items.stem: In an array implementation of a stack, what does the top of stack pointer hold?
options: The value of the top item
The index of the item most recently pushed
The index of the first item pushed
The number of free spaces
items.answer: The index of the item most recently pushed
items.markingKey: Push: increment pointer then store; pop: read then decrement.

items.stem: Explain why a linear queue implemented in an array can report that it is full even when it has empty spaces.
items.answer: Dequeued items leave spaces at the front, but the rear pointer has reached the end of the array, so no more items can be added unless the queue wraps around (circular) or items are shuffled.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each [2]

items.stem: Explain the purpose of the MOD operator when updating the pointers of a circular queue.
items.answer: When a pointer reaches the last index, (Pointer + 1) MOD Size returns it to index 0, so the array is used circularly.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each [2]

items.stem: Isla is writing an undo feature for a drawing app developed in Cairo, using a stack stored in an array. (a) Write pseudocode for a procedure Enqueue that adds an item to a circular queue of size 10, reporting when it is full. (b) Explain why a stack is suitable for an undo feature.
items.answer:
(a) PROCEDURE Enqueue(Item : STRING)
    IF NumberOfItems = 10 THEN
        OUTPUT "Queue full"
    ELSE
        RearPointer ← (RearPointer + 1) MOD 10
        Queue[RearPointer] ← Item
        NumberOfItems ← NumberOfItems + 1
    ENDIF
ENDPROCEDURE (b) The most recent action must be undone first (LIFO).
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark full check; 1 mark pointer update with MOD; 1 mark store item; 1 mark increment count [4] (b) 1 mark each [2]

items.stem: Why is a circular queue used instead of a linear queue in an array?
options: It keeps the items sorted
It allows items to be removed from the rear
Spaces freed at the front can be reused when the rear pointer wraps around
It needs no pointers
items.answer: Spaces freed at the front can be reused when the rear pointer wraps around
items.markingKey: Rear ← (Rear + 1) MOD Size.

items.stem: Assertion (A): A stack is first in, first out. Reason (R): Positions freed at the front of the array can be reused. Which option is correct?
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
items.answer: A is false but R is true
items.markingKey: A is false: "A stack is first in, first out." is incorrect; R is a true statement.

items.stem:
Isla has written this subroutine for an array-based ADT:
PROCEDURE Enqueue(Item : INTEGER)
    IF NumberOfItems = QueueSize THEN
        OUTPUT "Queue full"
    ELSE
        RearPointer ← RearPointer + 1
        Queue[RearPointer] ← Item
        NumberOfItems ← NumberOfItems + 1
    ENDIF
ENDPROCEDURE
Identify the error, explain its effect and give the correction.
items.answer: RearPointer ← RearPointer + 1 does not wrap round: it should be RearPointer ← (RearPointer + 1) MOD QueueSize. Effect: RearPointer goes beyond the last index (array out of bounds) instead of returning to 0.
items.markingKey: 1 mark error; 1 mark effect; 1 mark correction [3]

items.stem: A print server at Pioneer Insurance in Bogotá stores print jobs in a circular queue. (a) Write pseudocode for a function Pop that returns the top item of a stack, or −1 if the stack is empty. (b) Explain why a queue rather than a stack is suitable for print jobs.
items.answer:
(a) FUNCTION Pop() RETURNS INTEGER
    DECLARE Item : INTEGER
    IF TopOfStack = -1 THEN
        RETURN -1
    ELSE
        Item ← Stack[TopOfStack]
        TopOfStack ← TopOfStack - 1
        RETURN Item
    ENDIF
ENDFUNCTION (b) Jobs should be printed in the order they arrive (FIFO); a stack would print the newest job first.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark empty check; 1 mark read item; 1 mark decrement; 1 mark return [4] (b) 1 mark each [2]

items.stem: What does the start pointer of a linked list hold?
options: The index (address) of the first node in the list
The next free node
The number of nodes
The data in the last node
items.answer: The index (address) of the first node in the list
items.markingKey: A value of −1 (null) means the list is empty.

items.stem: Explain the advantage of a linked list over an array for a list that changes often.
items.answer: Items can be inserted and deleted by changing pointers only, without moving other items; the list can grow/shrink dynamically.

items.stem: Explain why a linked list cannot be searched with a binary search.
items.answer: Nodes can only be accessed by following pointers from the start; there is no direct access to the middle item.

At the root

items.stem: Explain why searching a balanced binary search tree is faster than searching an unordered list.
items.answer: Each comparison discards half of the remaining tree, so about log₂ n comparisons are needed instead of up to n.

items.stem: Explain why the order in which values are inserted affects the shape of a binary search tree.
items.answer: Each value is placed by comparison with existing nodes; inserting sorted data creates a tall, unbalanced tree like a linked list, which is slow to search.

items.stem:
Chloe has written this subroutine for an array-based ADT:
FUNCTION Dequeue() RETURNS INTEGER
    DECLARE Item : INTEGER
    Item ← Queue[FrontPointer]
    FrontPointer ← (FrontPointer + 1) MOD QueueSize

items.stem: A print server at Riverside Medical Centre in Riyadh stores print jobs in a circular queue. (a) Write pseudocode for a function Pop that returns the top item of a stack, or −1 if the stack is empty. (b) Explain why a stack is suitable for an undo feature.
items.answer:
(a) FUNCTION Pop() RETURNS INTEGER
    DECLARE Item : INTEGER
    IF TopOfStack = -1 THEN
        RETURN -1
    ELSE
        Item ← Stack[TopOfStack]
        TopOfStack ← TopOfStack - 1
        RETURN Item
    ENDIF
ENDFUNCTION (b) The most recent action must be undone first (LIFO).
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark empty check; 1 mark read item; 1 mark decrement; 1 mark return [4] (b) 1 mark each [2]

items.stem:
Diego has written this subroutine for an array-based ADT:
FUNCTION Pop() RETURNS INTEGER
    DECLARE Item : INTEGER
    TopOfStack ← TopOfStack - 1
    Item ← Stack[TopOfStack]
    RETURN Item
ENDFUNCTION

items.answer: TopOfStack is decremented before the item is read, so the wrong item is returned (and no underflow check); read Stack[TopOfStack] first, then decrement. Effect: The item below the top is returned and the top item is lost.

items.stem: A print server at SwiftCar Rentals in Toronto stores print jobs in a circular queue. (a) Write pseudocode for a procedure Enqueue that adds an item to a circular queue of size 10, reporting when it is full. (b) Explain why a stack is suitable for an undo feature.
items.answer:
(a) PROCEDURE Enqueue(Item : STRING)
    IF NumberOfItems = 10 THEN
        OUTPUT "Queue full"
    ELSE
        RearPointer ← (RearPointer + 1) MOD 10
        Queue[RearPointer] ← Item
        NumberOfItems ← NumberOfItems + 1
    ENDIF
ENDPROCEDURE (b) The most recent action must be undone first (LIFO).
